MEASURED 2026-08-13 by experiment on a scratch graph, because the answer could not be read off the schema and reading `get_node`'s signature only hints at it.

THE QUESTION Anthony asked: does each node within a graph have a unique id? THE ANSWER: no — the unique key is (node_type, node_id), not node_id alone.

WHAT WAS RUN. Created `thing:same` as a Capability and again as a Requirement in one graph: BOTH PERSISTED and both read back independently, with their own names. Then created `thing:same` as a Capability a second time: it MERGED with no error — the property passed overwrote, the `name` omitted survived, and `scan_nodes` reported one Capability. The storage key is `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}`, which is why `get_node` demands a type as well as an id.

⭐ THREE LEVELS, AND ONLY THE MIDDLE ONE IS ENFORCED:
  · `graph_id` ACROSS STORES — NOT unique, nothing checks it (see fact:two-adopted-stores-share-one-graph-id-2026-08-13)
  · (type, id) WITHIN a graph — unique BY CONSTRUCTION, it is the storage key
  · `id` ALONE within a graph — NOT unique; only the `cap:` / `req:` / `dec:` prefix convention keeps it clean

THE CONVENTION HOLDS IN PRACTICE AND IS NOT ENFORCED: across all 2,113 nodes of reflow2's own design, ZERO ids appear under more than one node type. Three types legitimately carry two prefixes each and none is a collision — Component `cmp:` (48) plus `sys:` (8, the functional systems from dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition); Decision `dec:` (222) plus `decision:` (126, the generated review-acknowledgement records); Contributor `who:` (5) plus ONE lingering `ctr:`, the residue of the Contributor fork.

🛑 WHY IT MATTERS FOR FEDERATION, and this is the asymmetry worth keeping: reflow2 is careful about id collisions ONE LEVEL DOWN and has nothing one level up. `mirror_surface` REFUSES a colliding node id and leaves the local node untouched, on the stated ground that "two designs using one id for different things is a naming conversation between their owners." The same hazard between two DESIGNS is a silent overwrite in a BTreeMap. Node collisions are a conversation; graph collisions are data loss.
